specification.title: MB1 — Ask where a place is at a train station
specification.learner_outcome: Given a clear visual and auditory situation in a UK train station, a beginning learner identifies the need to find the toilet, directly constructs and orally asks a relevant, functionally intelligible location question in English, responds to guidance with an improved own attempt, and transfers the question to finding an exit in a different nearby setting with less support. The learning entry is Pre-A1 toward initial A1; level A1 is the schema-level designation, not a claim of attained A1 mastery.

skills.description: Understand a simple everyday need to find a place and independently ask where it is in spoken English, using guidance to retry and applying the request to a nearby variation with reduced support.

required_evidence: Before the first comprehension question, the learner observes the approved station visual and hears an authorised, genuinely audible situation cue that does not name the required destination or reveal the answer. A visual alone, a written instruction, or an unverified playback path does not demonstrate the required audiovisual comprehension.

The learner makes an own recorded oral request for the toilet that is relevant to the situation and reviewable for functional intelligibility; the evidence attempt is made without a visible complete sentence model, Spanish prompt or transcript.

A distinct, relevant guidance event, derived from the learner's own recorded attempt and limited to one authorised item, is observable and acknowledged BEFORE a separate retry; the guidance, its source, the learner's support level and the retry are traceable. If guidance is unavailable, do not claim that the guided-retry sequence was completed.

The learner orally requests the exit from a different nearby station-side passage without visible answer support; the earlier supported toilet request has one opening-word cue, while the retry and transfer have none. Store transfer separately and do not infer success from completion alone.
Deferred retrieval in a different context without a complete model is a later distinct check and is not treated as completed by the immediate experience.
lesson_scope: First proposed experience within MB1 — Understanding and expressing a need; this specification does not define the full macrobloque.
Everyday scenario: a beginner needs to find the toilet at a UK train station.
Learner journey: understand, discover, construct, speak, receive guidance, retry, transfer.
Build the request directly in English from the communicative intention; do not rely on translating a Spanish sentence or copying a complete model for final evidence.

Transfer scenario: the learner moves from the main station hall to a nearby side passage and needs to find the exit; the new communicative need is presented without a full model and with less support than the preceding guided retry.
Keep exposure, instruction, supported practice, own oral production, evidence and transfer distinguishable; defer retrieval to a separate later context.
language_scope: Main productive request: Where is the toilet, please?
Optional opening for politeness: Excuse me.
Transfer request: Where is the exit, please?

The target is one simple oral location-question pattern with toilet and exit, plus the optional politeness opening; do not require unapproved additional productive vocabulary or alternate question structures.
pronunciation_scope: Prioritize functional intelligibility of a short spoken request over phonetic perfection or accent imitation.
Support understandable delivery of Where is the toilet, please? and Where is the exit, please? in short speech blocks.
Provide usable, non-authoritative pronunciation guidance followed by an opportunity to retry.
Do not turn individual phonemes, accent scoring or automatic speech recognition into separate Skills or evidence of mastery.
content_constraints: Represent one integrated, observable oral communication Skill for this first experience; do not create separate Skills for grammar, vocabulary, comprehension or pronunciation.
Use the approved station-toilet need and transfer to finding an exit in a different nearby setting; do not reproduce the historical A1-U1 immediate-need mission or I need + noun content.
Use the approved main question and optional Excuse me. opening; avoid additional mandatory productive forms.
Reveal the communicative purpose through a beginner-comprehensible visual and auditory situation, then guide direct construction in English.
Allow discovery and supported practice, but remove a full sentence model before final own-production and transfer evidence.
Keep any Spanish rescue or transcript as optional, later support under applicable Strict Support Timing; neither can supply final production evidence.
Separate preparatory comprehension checking, own production, guidance, distinct retry and transfer evidence.
Guide a new attempt after feedback and reduce the support for transfer compared with supported production.
Treat qualitative relevance and intelligibility as reviewable by a human or authorized external reviewer; Qwen, STT or automatic scoring may not accredit them.
Do not claim Skill mastery, retention, curricular progress or deferred retrieval on the basis of immediate experience completion.
Do not reuse historical A1-U1 missions, conversations, exercises, evidence or LessonExperience content as new MB1 curricular content.

An audiovisual-comprehension claim is blocked until an authorised audible asset or supported playback path is verified in the actual learning experience; no audio approval or asset is implied by this draft.
Guidance must be observable and linked to the learner's prior attempt before retry; a stage acknowledgement alone does not prove helpful feedback occurred.
Support must decrease across the own request (two isolated anchors), the supported retry (one opening-word cue), and transfer (no visible answer cue).

acceptance_criteria: PedagogicalUnitSpecification parses this draft successfully with the current backend Pydantic contract; parsing alone is not human pedagogical approval.
The specification describes the first MB1 experience in the approved Pre-A1 to initial A1 learning entry, without claiming to define all MB1 content.
An understandable train-station scenario leads the learner to identify a need to find the toilet before composing a spoken request directly in English.
The main productive request is Where is the toilet, please?, with optional Excuse me.; the transfer is Where is the exit, please? in a different nearby setting.
The journey contains understanding, discovery, construction, own oral request, guidance, retry and nearby transfer with demonstrably reduced support.
Comprehension checking, own initial production, guidance, retry and transfer are distinct and reviewable; final oral evidence does not expose Spanish, transcript or a full sentence model.
Functional intelligibility and communicative relevance are reviewed through the authorized qualitative process, never automatically accredited by Qwen or STT.
The future candidate remains isolated from active curriculum, content tree and runtime pointers, and requires a separately authorized integration and execution validation.
No inference or candidate materialization begins until human review of this specification has approved the open choices, including provisional identifiers and constraints.
Actual opening audiovisual delivery is demonstrated before q1 using an authorised audible situation cue that does not name the destination; no unsupported audio identity may be invented.
An authorised, attempt-specific guidance event is evidenced before a distinct retry; a nominal feedback stage or empty feedback_plans alone does not satisfy this criterion.
The first own oral request has one opening-word cue; the guided retry and new-context transfer have no visible word cues. No full answer model is presented during scored oral evidence.

candidate_unit.title: Find a place at the station

lessons.title: Find a place at the station
lessons.objective: Find a place at a train station and transfer the request to finding the exit.

mission.title: Find help at the station
mission.situation: You are at a British train station and need help finding a place.
mission.observable_outcome: Make an own oral request for a place, retry after guidance, and ask for the exit with less support.
success_criteria: Choose the place needed in the station situation.
Make an own request for the chosen place.
Make a distinct retry after guidance.
Ask for the exit without visible answer support.

stages.instruction: Observe the station scene and listen to its authorised non-answer-revealing situation audio before choosing the place the passenger needs. If the audio is unavailable, the audiovisual requirement remains blocked rather than silently passing.
Notice the English chunks used to ask for a place.
Build the request directly from the English chunks.
Make your own oral request to a station worker using only the opening-word cue, never a complete example sentence.

After the learner's recorded request, present exactly one available authorised, attempt-specific guidance item (prioritise relevance and intelligibility), and capture that it was received before the next attempt. If no such item is available, do not claim guidance or a successful guided retry.
Retry the toilet request after the recorded guidance without visible word cues (less support than the opening-word cue shown for the first request).
Now in a different nearby side passage, ask a worker for the exit orally without any visible word cues or answer model; record this transfer separately.
